subject: 300 Factories Re-Training Loop at [COMPANY]
text:
Hi [NAME],

We were in conversation with Damjan earlier this year, and I'm reaching out
to you directly because the hiring you're doing tells a different story
about where the data infrastructure bottleneck is now.

You're bringing on an AI Scientist and ML Engineer focused on building
foundation models that generalise across factory environments with minimal
data. Having worked with Baker Hughes and Toyota this year, I know
first-hand that the constraint is the data layer, not how fast models can
be shipped.

At two customers, the retraining data loop was a manual process but
manageable. At 300 factories, with each environment adding its own defect
ontology and failure modes, the process of surfacing training examples and
closing the retraining cycle becomes the thing that wastes engineering time.

[SENDER]'s piece in The Manufacturer flags capturing tacit manufacturing
knowledge at scale as the goal. That only happens if your research team
spends time on the models, not the pipeline.

Worth a quick reconnect with you and the team about how to structure the
data layer so your new hires stay focused on the science?

subject: $500m Premium Imagery Labelling Problem
text:
Hi [NAME],

I spoke with a couple of people on your team this week. One mentioned they
have satellite imagery labelling work on their plate, with annotation split
between an internal team and third parties.

That disconnected workflow hits model accuracy directly, and model accuracy
is your competitive edge. We helped Tractable
<[LINK]>,
who assesses property damage from imagery for major insurers, scale to 40+
annotators while keeping quality control tight across complex ontologies.

Encord handles imagery, video, and time series in one platform, including
the on-site wind speed data you are now pulling.

With Germany and Austria now added and a $500M premium target on the
horizon, the labelling and curation burden only grows with each new region.
Do you have 20 minutes early next week to discuss further?

subject: Cortex launch. Seven agents. One eval problem.
text:
Hi [NAME]

I saw Cortex launched this week. Seven agents in production, drawing
interpretation live. Having worked with a few companies in the construction
AI space I know the constraint that limits how fast that compounds is
whether your team can close the loop between a wrong answer in the field
and a corrected example back in training, without wasting engineering time.

We work with companies like OnsightIQ and Appfolio, running document and
HITL evaluation pipelines at scale. From experience, I know that the
internal tooling that got you to launch stops scaling when agent count and
project volume both rise at the same time. Both companies hit 5x faster
data throughput and went from 2 months to 2 weeks to get a new project
operational.

Do you have 20 minutes next week for a quick conversation about how to
structure that layer so your engineers stay focused on models?

subject: Alpha Index. More data than ever. Data layer question.
text:
Hi [NAME],

We spoke with Julian on your team last year and he asked us to come back
when time series was more relevant on our end. Thought i'd flag to you as
well.

We work with agritech teams on the data infrastructure underneath their AI
models. I saw the LDV investor piece from February. Both the Bayer and the
Delphy results are a strong validation of what the platform is producing at
scale.

The data challenges that come with that scale, labelling stress events on
photosynthesis streams, curating which signals matter for model training,
are where we come in.

We have been investing heavily in time series support across the platform.
This covers visualisation of sensor streams alongside other data, 1D range
annotation for labelling events and intervals, and multi-channel support
for tabular CSV uploads.

Let me know if it's worth 20 minutes with your team to see if it fits your
sensor workflow?
